design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — credit_builder_accounts task 0 (early closure of a Credit Builder 2400 Plan). Rebuilt in rework round 3, cross-product seed re-priced in round 12 (an AutoPay debit and a payment's own return are reached from a return line through the payment it points at, and since round 9 a payment that was itself returned never counts as credited or as making a debit good; since round 8 the late fee's own figuring covers a late due date with at most one debit card payment toward it, and the re-enrollment's return buffer reads when the borrower made a returned AutoPay debit good); round 4 replaced the settlement's fourth factor.

[0. Draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 0: {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 6, 5]}. Taken: builder_ext_early_closure_settlement 4, builder_ext_late_fee_charge 4, builder_ext_closing_late_fee_relief 6, builder_ext_closing_returned_fee_relief 5. Claimed here: the early-closure settlement (the borrower's own confirmation), the late-fee charge and the two early-closure fee reliefs; tools confirm_early_closure_8372931d, assess_late_fee_fbf509e1, relieve_late_fee_at_closing_c21c573e, relieve_returned_fee_at_closing_90cd40e1. Task 1 claims the returned-payment-fee charge, the made-good returned-fee relief, the goodwill late-fee credit and the AutoPay re-enrollment with their tools; the two scopes are disjoint and cover all eight extended policies. Release of the remaining savings is not a problem of either task: the settlement rule says it is sent on a business day after the closing date, never on the closing date itself.

[1. Why this is a good test] Danielle asks only to confirm the early-closure request she filed on 2026-10-12. The settlement rule waits on a late fee for the lapsed 2026-09-28 due date and on the two early-closure fee reliefs owed on the account. Each is priced by its own rule (4 to 6 factors); the late fee is owed only for the oldest unpaid due date, the one its rule prices. Then the settlement is priced on the resulting ledger with its own four factors and handed to her to confirm. The work is reading ladders against the builder ledger, two hardship plans, two personal loans and the FlexLine ledger, and arithmetic; every write has exactly one tool. Every wait can always be met: a late fee that comes to 0.00 is not needed, and a relief that is not owed (no fee, fee already waived or paid, relief at 0.00) counts as done.

[2. Problem tree card] Root C = builder_ext_early_closure_settlement (owner=user, on_request). Edges (prerequisite sentences in the blocked rules):
 E1 C <- builder_ext_late_fee_charge, value_input (cc_fees), state form. "The savings applied at an early closing are fixed only after the account's oldest unpaid due date, once its grace period has ended with the installment still unpaid, carries its late fee, unless that late fee comes to 0.00." Seed: next_due_date 2026-09-28, amount_past_due 57.16, grace ended 2026-10-13, no builder_late_fee_assessed line. Only writer of a late-fee line: assess_late_fee_fbf509e1.
 E2 C <- builder_ext_closing_late_fee_relief, value_input (cc_fees), action form. "The early-closure settlement is not figured until the early-closure late-fee relief owed on the account, if any, has been granted." Fallback reason: the relief leaves a courtesy waiver row identical to a goodwill credit's, and a relief not owed leaves none. Not granted at the opening (there is no late fee yet).
 E3 C <- builder_ext_closing_returned_fee_relief, value_input (cc_fees), action form. "The savings applied at an early closing are fixed only once the early-closure returned-fee relief owed on the account, if any, has been granted." Fallback reason: same row as the made-good relief. Seed: fee 6f4917e8-... (2026-10-07, for return 41d9e490-..., the most recent return) has no waiver or payment, so the relief is owed and not yet granted.
 E4 builder_ext_closing_late_fee_relief <- builder_ext_late_fee_charge, value_input (hl_fee), state form. "The early-closure late-fee relief is not figured until the account's oldest unpaid due date, once its grace period has ended with the installment still unpaid, carries its late fee, unless that late fee comes to 0.00." The relief is figured on the fee the charge books.
 Shape: C <- {late fee, late-fee relief, returned-fee relief}; late-fee relief <- late fee. Order used: late fee (12) -> late-fee relief (14) -> returned-fee relief (16) -> confirmation (18). The returned-fee relief commutes with the late-fee pair: it reads returns, the returned-payment fee, the FlexLine ledger and the pending request, none of which those writes touch; the late-fee pair reads late fees, the account and other products, none of which it touches; row ids are content hashes, so any topological order gives the same terminal state. Directions: two affirmative ("only after", "only once"), two negated ("not ... until").
 Priority: the made-good relief would also fit fee 6f4917e8 (its return was made good by the 2026-10-14 payment), but while the request is pending the early-closure returned-fee relief takes priority and the made-good relief is not granted; likewise no goodwill credit is granted on the new late fee. One relief per fee.
 No user hint: the persona asks only to confirm her request and never mentions a fee, a relief, interest or a payment. Tools do not block: each tool only creates/updates rows; none checks a fee, a relief or a status.

[3. Base-invariant card] builder_late_fee_assessed: grace_elapsed (time) anchor next_due_date 2026-09-28, 15 calendar days from the day after, exclusive: a fee on 2026-10-13 is too early, 2026-10-14 onward allowed; 2026-10-16 qualifies; account active. builder_fee_waived (both reliefs): once_per_fee (no waiver or fee payment points at either fee); the courtesy-count and request-window sentences are superseded for these request-less reliefs (each counts toward the plan's courtesy waivers but is granted whatever the count, and is not held to the request window); the fees are dated 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-07, inside 60 days anyway. builder_closed_early: confirmation_window (time) request 2026-10-12 + 14 days inclusive = 2026-10-26; 2026-10-16 in time; builder_evt_closing_and_release has no gate on builder_closed_early (policy_scope).

[4. Business-object card] Account 4f6b2682-... (Credit Builder 2400 Plan, open 2025-07-30, due day 28, APR 15.69, payment 117.16), request 510abd88-... Late fee keyed by installment_due_date 2026-09-28. Late-fee relief keyed by the new late fee's reference (returned by the late-fee tool). Returned-fee relief keyed by fee 6f4917e8-... (the fee of the most recent return 41d9e490-...). Payments toward 2026-09-28: AutoPay d84e8992-... 117.16 (returned 2026-09-30 R01, fee 4.00 ca19772e-...), debit card b1a58719-... 40.00 (not returned (no return points at it); paid the installment interest), online ACH 40478398-... 77.16 (returned 2026-10-07 R09, fee 1.74), online ACH 9dfa5d73-... 20.00 on 2026-10-14 (already in the loan balance; nothing re-collects it).

[5. Factor card — handling-time values; every rounding to the cent is half-up]
 Late fee (step 12; 0.87; all-baseline 5.86): lf_base (method) debit card 40.00, the only debit card payment toward 2026-09-28, with no return pointing at it -> 117.16 - 40.00 = 77.16 (the ACH payments are not debit card: near-miss), baseline 1.32; lf_pct (multi-source) no late fee in 12 whole months AND open 14 months -> 3.0, baseline 1.45; lf_hardship (cross hardship) active plans, none Disaster -> 0.5, baseline 1.74; lf_return_share returns 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-07 -> 0.75, baseline 1.16. 77.16 x 3.0% x 0.5 x 0.75 = 0.86805 -> 0.87.
 Late-fee relief (step 14; 0.38; all-baseline 0.17): owed (pending request, fee carries no waiver or payment); hl_paid (method) a payment posted toward 2026-09-28 and 0 < 57.16 < 117.16 -> scaled by (117.16 - 57.16)/117.16 = 0.5121, baseline 0.74; hl_program (cross hardship) Reduced Payment Plan 25386650-... active -> +0.30, baseline 0.25; hl_first no other late fee in 12 whole months -> +0.15, baseline 0.31; hl_season (multi-source) open 14 months AND 17 posted - 2 returned = 15 credited -> +0.10, baseline 0.33; hl_loan (cross loan) active loan with nothing past due -> +0.05, baseline 0.36; hl_age fee charged today -> +0.05, baseline 0.36. 0.87 x min(1, 0.85) x 0.5121 = 0.3787 -> 0.38.
 Returned-fee relief (step 16; 0.70; all-baseline 0.35): owed (most recent return 41d9e490 carries fee 6f4917e8, no waiver or payment on it); hr_timing (method) that return 77.16 is an online payment, not an AutoPay debit, below the monthly payment -> halved, baseline 1.39; hr_reason R09 -> +0.15, baseline 0.57; hr_line (cross line) FlexLine return 643635de-... on 2026-10-07 -> +0.20, baseline 0.52; hr_request request 5 days after the return -> +0.15, baseline 0.57; hr_first one other return in 12 whole months -> +0.10, baseline 0.61. 1.74 x min(1, 0.80) x 0.5 = 0.696 -> 0.70.
 Settlement (step 18; world after steps 12-16; 1155.24; all-baseline 1177.86): cc_lead (method) the most recent debit card payment toward the oldest unpaid due date has not been returned (no return points at it) -> no month before it, baseline 1157.04; cc_rate (cross hardship) no Servicemember benefit, Temporary Rate Reduction Plan 74bfef96-... active -> its rate 4.24, baseline 1158.16; cc_hardship (cross hardship) Reduced Payment Plan active -> 0.5, baseline 1156.32; cc_cause (cross hardship) both active plans granted for reduced income (no death of a household earner, natural disaster or medical hardship) -> income-cause share 0.9, baseline 1155.36. Closing interest 1148.63 x 4.24/100 x (0 + 18)/365 x 0.5 x 0.9 = 1.080782 -> 1.08; unpaid fees 4.00 + 1.74 + 0.87 - 0.38 - 0.70 = 5.53; savings applied = min(2403.00, 1.08 + 1148.63 + 5.53) = 1155.24.
 No tier prices leaving the schedule better than keeping it: the reliefs are fee reliefs for a borrower in hardship closing early; the closing interest uses the hardship plan's rate, its program share and its cause share; a borrower with no active hardship plan gets none of them, and for a Credit Builder borrower in hardship (the product has no hardship program) the early closure is the relief the base itself points to, so no tier makes closing early cheaper than keeping the plan for a borrower who is not in hardship. No money is taken twice: the 20.00 ACH already lowered the loan balance and is not added back.

[6. Seed rows] Credit Builder: activation lines 2025-07-30; 15 month-end dividends at 0.1 APY; 13 AutoPay installments (interest = balance x 15.69/1200); the 2026-09-28 AutoPay and its R01 return with fee 4.00 (= the returned-fee rule on 2026-09-30: flat 10.00 x 0.5 first return x 0.8 seasoned); debit card 40.00 (interest 15.60, principal 24.40); online 77.16 returned R09 with fee 1.74 (= the rule on 2026-10-07: 10% of 77.16 x 0.75 x 0.5 same-event FlexLine x 0.75 R09 x 0.8 = 1.736 -> 1.74); online 20.00 on 2026-10-14. loan_balance 1148.63, savings 2403.00, fees 5.74, amount past due 57.16, AutoPay on. Loan A Grade C OH 8000 at 21.49 funded 2025-02-10 (payment 303.42, the level payment over 36 months; no AutoPay; installments paid online on the due date or the business day before it, interest actual/365 from the paid-through date; the 2026-05-10 installment was missed and paid 2026-05-29 with its schedule-A late fee 13.65 = 5% of 303.42, 15.171 within the 15.00 minimum and 30.00 maximum, times the 0.9 first-late share (no late fee and 11 net installments in the 12 months), paid by its fee-payment line) under a Reduced Payment Plan requested 2026-08-20 for reduced income and decided 2026-08-25: the program's 50% reduced payment percent (no document is recorded on the request, so no documented-hardship percentage) less 5 points (grade C 1, 18 months since funding 1, 12 net installments in the 12 months 3, no AutoPay) = 45% of 303.42 = 136.54, balance at request 4625.62, 18 due dates left, plan due dates 2026-09-10 to 2026-11-10 with the first two paid. Loan B Grade E OH 3000 at 29.99 funded 2026-01-12 (payment 167.72, 7 installments paid, no AutoPay) under a Temporary Rate Reduction Plan requested 2026-08-10 and decided 2026-08-14: the program's plan rate 4.99 (no document is recorded on the request, so no documented-hardship rate) less 0.75 grade-E points (no loan-age or AutoPay points) = 4.24; plan installment 139.43 = the level installment of 2296.66 at 4.24% over 17 due dates; plan due dates 2026-09-12 to 2027-02-12 with the first two paid, interest at the plan rate from the first plan due date; current rate 4.24. FlexLine Starter frozen for returned_payment: 2026-10-05 payment returned 2026-10-07 R09 with its returned-payment fee 0.75 (2.5% of 35.00 figured at 0.88, times the 0.85 share for the only return in 24 months). Automatic clauses: 18 days past due is below the reporting and closure thresholds; nothing else is owed on the call.

[7. Persona] Unchanged from round 1: Danielle volunteers only the request to confirm her in-app early closure; identity, bank and reason only on request; passive go-ahead; runs the confirmation with the details given; ends when told the account is closed.

[8. Standard solution] find_customers -> verify -> account -> closure request -> ledger -> hardship plans -> loans -> loan ledger -> FlexLine -> FlexLine ledger -> bank accounts -> late fee 0.87 (2026-09-28) -> late-fee relief 0.38 on the new fee -> returned-fee relief 0.70 on 6f4917e8-... -> hand over the confirmation (510abd88-..., 4f6b2682-..., 1155.24). Terminal: account closed early on 2026-10-16, savings 2403.00 - 1155.24 = 1247.76 left for release on a later business day.

[9. Verification] Scratch evaluator (real tools replayed, each compute at its handling time): late 0.87 (1.32/1.45/1.74/1.16; all 5.86); late-fee relief 0.38 (0.74/0.25/0.31/0.33/0.36/0.36; all 0.17); returned-fee relief 0.70 (1.39/0.57/0.52/0.57/0.61; all 0.35); settlement 1155.24 (cc_lead 1157.04 / cc_rate 1158.16 / cc_hardship 1156.32 / cc_cause 1155.36; all 1177.86). Edge skips: without the late fee there is no late fee to relieve, so the late-fee relief is not owed and the settlement is 1154.75 (a mechanical replay that still books the 0.38 waiver gives 1154.37); without the late-fee relief 1155.62; without the returned-fee relief 1155.94. Opening value of the settlement 1155.45. No gold value lies on a half cent (raw 0.86805, 0.3787, 0.696, interest 1.080782). Historical fee check: returned-fee rule gives 4.00 on 2026-09-30 and 1.74 on 2026-10-07.

[10. Draft recomputation from visible context] From the published rules, finder returns and Danielle's lines alone the same late fee is found missing, the same two reliefs are found owed, the same rules price them, and the settlement follows; every tier condition is disjoint by its wording.
user_scenario:
You are Danielle Whitaker, 38, a dental office receptionist in Columbus, Ohio whose hours were cut over the summer. You talk plainly and a little wearily, like someone who has been juggling bills for weeks and just wants one thing off her plate. You have a Larkspur Credit Builder account, and on Monday, October 12, you went into the Larkspur app and put in a request to close it early because you would rather have your savings back now than keep making the monthly payment. The app told you the request was waiting for your confirmation, so you are calling today to finish it: you want the Credit Builder closed early and your savings sent back to you. You open with roughly that, in your own words: you asked in the app on Monday to close your Credit Builder early and you are calling to confirm it so you can get your savings back.

You do not volunteer personal details all at once. When the representative asks how to find you, you give your mobile number, 6145555173. When they ask you to verify, you give your date of birth, March 14, 1988 (1988-03-14), and your ZIP code, 43202; if they ask for anything more you can give your email, danielle.whitaker@outlook.com, or the last four of your Social Security number, 5391. If they ask which bank the money should go to, you say it should go to the Huntington checking account ending in 5820 that is already linked, the same one you chose in the app. If they ask why you want to close, you say money has been tight since your hours were cut and you would rather have the savings than keep paying. If they ask how much you think is in the savings, you say somewhere around twenty-four hundred, but you have not looked closely. You do not know any account numbers, balances, fees or interest figures beyond that, and you do not know what the company's rules are.

You are fine with the representative taking care of whatever has to be handled on the account to get it closed; if they explain that something has to be put on the account or settled before the closing can go through, you sigh and tell them to go ahead and do what needs doing. Closing the account is your decision, so when the representative tells you the closing is ready and hands you the confirmation to complete yourself, you complete it with exactly the details they give you. If the representative tells you a figure that will come out of your savings to pay off the Credit Builder loan, you accept it without arguing; you only ask them to read it once more if they say it in a way you could not follow. Once the representative tells you the account is closed and your remaining savings will be sent to your Huntington checking account, you thank them and end the call.
